model-sourcing.title: Sourcing a Model Under Contract
model-sourcing.question: Faced with a modeling task, can an agent SOURCE the model well — reuse an existing module, compose several, or build a new one when justified — and can that sourcing decision be held to a contract that rewards reuse, catches reinvention, and refuses a module that does not actually fit?
model-sourcing.hypothesis: Each task's required capabilities and each module's declared capabilities are enough to grade the sourcing decision deterministically (requires ⊆ capabilities), so reuse-when-you-should and build-only-when-warranted become enforced axes, not hopes.
model-sourcing.lead: Six modeling tasks, three real installed modules (viva-munk, spatio-flux, viva-cpm), and a deterministic sourcing audit that grades every reuse / compose / build-new decision — including a trap where a plausible-but-wrong module is caught.

executive.what_is_this: This investigation extends the model-build-under-contract loop with a SELECT phase: before the tests are locked, the agent decides WHERE the model comes from. Each of six tasks declares the capabilities it requires; three real modules declare the capabilities they provide; the module_sourcing audit grades the decision on four axes (source_fit, reinvention, novelty_justified, survey_recorded).
executive.verdict: The audit graded all six tasks correctly: 5 pass and the deliberate trap (TRAP-wrong-reuse) FAILS on source_fit because viva-munk provides no `spatial` capability. All three reused modules execute for real on ONE shared workspace core (viva-munk rigid-body physics; spatio-flux spatial dFBA with real glucose drawdown and acetate secretion; viva-cpm Cellular Potts cells relaxing toward their target shape) — each is inherited into viva_casebook.core.build_core rather than run on a parallel core. Only the two non-reuse tasks (build-new, trap) have no run, by design.

at_a_glance.role: compose → compose growth-proc + viva-munk · audit PASS
reuse → no clean fit — needs `spatial`, which viva-munk lacks · audit FAIL

agentic-challenges.title: Hard agentic-modeling challenges
agentic-challenges.question: Which modeling tasks genuinely require an LLM agent — where a deterministic policy has no move for the real fix — and can the agent build a passing process-bigraph model for them?
agentic-challenges.hypothesis: As task complexity moves from calibration → regulatory coupling → simulator selection + subcellular composition, the deterministic policy fails while an LLM agent reasons the fix.
agentic-challenges.lead: A benchmark suite: each task is a real composite, graded by locked tests, with an LLM-vs-deterministic-policy head-to-head. See docs/agentic-tasks-roadmap.md.

studies.title: Bounded goal-directed cell
studies.question: Build a bounded, goal-directed cell: on a finite nutrient pool and a rising temperature, produce a cell whose BIOMASS grows on the nutrient it CONSUMES (mass-conserving, Monod-saturating GROWTH), and whose VIABILITY holds while below its temperature tolerance then collapses once temperature exceeds it.
studies.biological_summary: A process-bigraph Composite: TemperatureRamp + MonodUptake + YieldGrowth + ThermalDeath (t_tol=43 °C), wired over stores biomass/nutrient/viability/temperature/uptake_flux.
studies.conclusion:
## Final model
A process-bigraph Composite: TemperatureRamp + MonodUptake + YieldGrowth + ThermalDeath (t_tol=43 °C), wired over stores biomass/nutrient/viability/temperature/uptake_flux.

## Result
DONE in 4 edits (LLM agent) — a real process-bigraph composite, integrity clean. The deterministic policy also solved it in 5.

agent_trajectory.driver: LLM agent (Claude Sonnet) — decisions reasoned live from graded verdicts
agent_trajectory.contract: Build a bounded, goal-directed cell: on a finite nutrient pool and a rising temperature, produce a cell whose BIOMASS grows on the nutrient it CONSUMES (mass-conserving, Monod-saturating GROWTH), and whose VIABILITY holds while below its temperature tolerance then collapses once temperature exceeds it.

decision.reasoning: Growth and nutrient-depletion both require consuming nutrient via a Monod uptake flux before biomass conversion can happen, and monod_uptake is the upstream dependency yield_growth needs, so install it first.
Conservation and growth are both failing because the uptake flux from monod_uptake has nowhere to go — yield_growth converts consumed nutrient into biomass, closing the mass balance.
viability-cliff requires viability to collapse once temperature exceeds tolerance, which is exactly what thermal_death models and no mechanism for that is installed yet.

t_tol=35 is below the starting temperature so decay starts at t=0 and kills viability before t=3h; raising t_tol above the t=3h temperature (~42 °C) delays onset past the in-band checkpoint while still collapsing viability before the 50 °C peak.
All five hard tests read within_tol — the model is built; report DONE rather than edit further.

studies.title: Multicellular differentiation phenotype
studies.question: Produce a multicellular tissue with a spatial differentiation gradient: cells near a signalling niche stay stem, distal cells differentiate.
studies.biological_summary: A CPM (viva-cpm) tissue Composite: a Wnt-secreting niche + progenitor cells on the lattice, a diffusing Wnt field, and a StemnessFate subcell reading each cell's local Wnt to set its fate — producing a spatial differentiation gradient.

behavior_tests.name: simulator-fit
behavior_tests.description: The chosen simulator supports lattice + fields + cell fate

behavior_tests.name: differentiation-gradient
behavior_tests.description: Stem near the niche, differentiated distally

studies.conclusion:
## Final model
A CPM (viva-cpm) tissue Composite: a Wnt-secreting niche + progenitor cells on the lattice, a diffusing Wnt field, and a StemnessFate subcell reading each cell's local Wnt to set its fate — producing a spatial differentiation gradient.

## Result
The phenotype (near STEM, far DIFFERENTIATED) is produced by the CPM composite. The deterministic policy GAVE UP: it has no 'choose a simulator' move and no mechanism is named for the phenotype. Selecting CPM + composing the subcell is the LLM's job.

agent_trajectory.driver: LLM agent (Claude Sonnet) — selected the simulator + composed the subcell model
agent_trajectory.contract: Produce a multicellular tissue with a spatial differentiation GRADIENT: cells near a signalling niche stay stem, and cells farther away differentiate — a tissue-scale phenotype, not a single-cell property.

violations: I1: locked behavior_tests changed outside a re-open→AUDIT round

decision.reasoning: Only cpm supports lattice + morphogen fields + cell-fate relabeling, which the differentiation-gradient phenotype requires (pymunk has none; spatial has fields but no fate).
The Wnt niche field must exist before per-cell fate can sense it, so add the niche/field first.
Cells need the subcellular fate model that reads local Wnt to relabel stem vs differentiated, producing the spatial gradient.
All three tests pass — CPM with the niche field and the fate subcell produces the gradient.

policy_trajectory.contract: Produce a multicellular tissue with a spatial differentiation GRADIENT: cells near a signalling niche stay stem, and cells farther away differentiate — a tissue-scale phenotype, not a single-cell property.

studies.question: Build an SBML kinetic model of a linear metabolic pathway A→B→C that COPASI can load and simulate to a valid steady state, with total mass conserved and the terminal product C accumulating as the dominant species.

studies.conclusion:
## Final model
An SBML kinetic model of A→B→C (mass-action), loaded + simulated in COPASI (basico) via viva-copasi.

## Result
DONE (5/5) — the LLM agent authored the reaction network, recognising after A→B that the pathway stopped at B and adding B→C so the terminal product accumulates. studies.title: Multiscale coupling via a translator
studies.question: Couple a cell-scale metabolic model (which produces a metabolite FLUX) to a tissue-scale spatial DIFFUSION FIELD of that metabolite, so that the cell's secretion sources the field and a gradient forms around the cell — with mass conserved across the scale interface.
studies.biological_summary: A two-scale process-bigraph Composite: CellMetabolism (a cell secreting a metabolite flux, mol/time) + DiffusionField (a 1-D concentration field, mM) coupled by a FluxTranslator that maps the cell's flux to the field's per-grid source with the unit conversion (÷volume) that conserves mass across the scale interface.
studies.conclusion:
## Final model
A two-scale process-bigraph Composite: CellMetabolism (a cell secreting a metabolite flux, mol/time) + DiffusionField (a 1-D concentration field, mM) coupled by a FluxTranslator that maps the cell's flux to the field's per-grid source with the unit conversion (÷volume) that conserves mass across the scale interface.

## Result
DONE (4/4) — the LLM agent recognised the two models were decoupled and AUTHORED a translator, reasoning the unit conversion (mol/time → mM/time over the compartment volume) needed to conserve mass. The deterministic policy GAVE UP at 1/4: 'author a translator' is not an install it can express. See docs/multiscale-agent-vs-policy.html.

agent_trajectory.driver: LLM agent (Claude Sonnet) — authored the translator + reasoned the unit conversion
agent_trajectory.contract: Couple a cell-scale metabolic model (which produces a metabolite FLUX) to a tissue-scale spatial DIFFUSION FIELD of that metabolite, so that the cell's secretion sources the field and a gradient forms around the cell — with mass conserved across the scale interface.

violations: I1: locked behavior_tests changed outside a re-open→AUDIT round

decision.reasoning: Start with the cell-scale source model before anything can secrete.
The tissue-scale field must exist before it can respond.

The two models are unconnected until a translator maps secretion_flux to field_source; units differ (mol/time vs mM/time over volume V=2.0) so the conversion must be applied for mass to conserve across the interface.
All four tests pass — the translator couples the two scales and conserves mass.

studies.title: Ambiguous diagnosis (why is biomass low?)
studies.question: A cell's biomass is far below target. Diagnose the cause from the observables and add the mechanism that fixes it, so the cell both grows (biomass >= 3.0) and stays alive (viability >= 0.5).
studies.biological_summary: A process-bigraph Composite: CellGrowth (Monod uptake → yield growth, GATED by viability) + MembraneStress (viability decay). Biomass is low because the cell is DYING, not because of yield or uptake — a cause diagnosable only from the joint observables (nutrient fully consumed, viability crashed). The fix is stabilize_membrane.
studies.conclusion:
## Final model
A process-bigraph Composite: CellGrowth (Monod uptake → yield growth, GATED by viability) + MembraneStress (viability decay). Biomass is low because the cell is DYING, not because of yield or uptake — a cause diagnosable only from the joint observables (nutrient fully consumed, viability crashed). The fix is stabilize_membrane.

## Result
DONE (2/2) in 1 edit — the LLM read the joint observable panel (nutrient fully consumed → uptake fine; viability crashed → cell dying) and installed the one correct fix. The deterministic policy MISDIAGNOSED: it hill-climbed the worst margin, installed boost_yield, growth still failed, and it gave up — a low-growth margin alone cannot name the cause. See docs/diagnosis-agent-vs-policy.html.

agent_trajectory.driver: LLM agent (Claude) — diagnosed the cause from the joint observable panel
agent_trajectory.contract: A cell's biomass is far below target. Diagnose the cause from the observables and add the mechanism that fixes it, so the cell both grows (biomass >= 3.0) and stays alive (viability >= 0.5).

violations: I1: locked behavior_tests changed outside a re-open→AUDIT round

decision.reasoning: The panel diagnoses the cause: nutrient is fully consumed (uptake is fine) and yield is adequate, yet biomass is low BECAUSE viability has crashed to ~0 — the cell dies before it can grow. This is membrane failure, not a yield or uptake deficit, so boosting either would not help. Install stabilize_membrane to keep the cell alive; growth follows.
Both tests pass — the cell survives (viability held) and grows past the biomass target. The diagnosis (membrane failure) was correct.

policy_trajectory.contract: A cell's biomass is far below target. Diagnose the cause from the observables and add the mechanism that fixes it, so the cell both grows (biomass >= 3.0) and stays alive (viability >= 0.5).

studies.title: Bistable genetic switch
studies.question: Build a bistable genetic switch: two mutually repressing genes A and B that settle into two DISTINCT stable states and latch to whichever gene starts ahead (a decisive toggle, not a graded midpoint).
studies.biological_summary: A process-bigraph Composite: a ToggleSwitch process — two mutually repressing genes A,B with COOPERATIVE (Hill n=2) repression. Cooperativity is the structural feature that destabilises the symmetric state and opens two stable basins, so the switch latches to whichever gene starts ahead.
studies.conclusion:
## Final model
A process-bigraph Composite: a ToggleSwitch process — two mutually repressing genes A,B with COOPERATIVE (Hill n=2) repression. Cooperativity is the structural feature that destabilises the symmetric state and opens two stable basins, so the switch latches to whichever gene starts ahead.

## Result
DONE (2/2) in 1 edit — the LLM recognised that two stable states require COOPERATIVE feedback (Hill n≥2) and added it, opening two basins (state separation 3.46). The deterministic policy tuned expression (a knob), stayed monostable (separation 0), and gave up: bistability is a structural property no single knob tunes into being. See docs/bistable-agent-vs-policy.html.

agent_trajectory.driver: LLM agent (Claude) — recognised bistability requires cooperative feedback
agent_trajectory.contract: Build a bistable genetic switch: two mutually repressing genes A and B that settle into two DISTINCT stable states and latch to whichever gene starts ahead (a decisive toggle, not a graded midpoint).

violations: I1: locked behavior_tests changed outside a re-open→AUDIT round

decision.reasoning: Both genes relax to the same symmetric level — the switch is monostable, and boosting expression or degradation only moves that single fixed point, never splits it. Two stable states in a mutual-repression network require COOPERATIVE repression (Hill n >= 2): ultrasensitivity is what destabilises the symmetric state and opens two basins. Install cooperative_binding.
Both tests pass — the two initial conditions latch to distinct, decisive states (A-high vs B-high). Cooperative feedback produced the bistability.

policy_trajectory.contract: Build a bistable genetic switch: two mutually repressing genes A and B that settle into two DISTINCT stable states and latch to whichever gene starts ahead (a decisive toggle, not a graded midpoint).
